title: World Youth Championships day six: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi win mixed gold as two fourth seeds fall
seo_title: World Youth Championships day 6: Wen and Jiang win mixed
description: World Youth Championships day six: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi won the U19 mixed doubles, France beat two fourth seeds and Yao Ruixuan came from 3-0 down.
standfirst: Antoine Noirault and Leana Hochart knocked out the fourth seeds in the U19 singles last 16, and Yao Ruixuan came from three games down before losing the mixed final.
body: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi won the first under-19 individual title of the World Youth Championships in Istanbul on Thursday, beating their China teammates Li Hechen and Yao Ruixuan 4-11, 11-4, 11-6, 11-4 in the mixed doubles final.

It was China's third under-19 gold of the week after both team titles on Monday, and Wen and Jiang, seeded only 16th, can still win four each. Earlier, France's Antoine Noirault and Leana Hochart knocked out the fourth seeds in the boys' and girls' singles, and Yao came from three games down to reach the girls' quarter-finals.
## Wen and Jiang take the mixed title

Li and Yao, the second seeds, won the first game of the final 11-4 and looked the sharper pair. Wen and Jiang then won 33 of the next 47 points, taking the last three games 11-4, 11-6 and 11-4. Li and Yao called their timeout but could not stop the run, and the final lasted 26 minutes.

Wen, 19, is the world No 14 and the highest-ranked player in Istanbul; Jiang turned 16 last week. They had beaten Japan's Kohaku Nakano and Aoba Takahashi in straight games in Tuesday's semi-final. On Friday both play singles quarter-finals, and then Wen plays the boys' doubles final with Li and Jiang the girls' doubles final with Yao.
## Yao's long day

Yao played three times and was taken the distance twice. Russia's Eseniia Shirokova, ranked 414th, led their last-16 match 3-0 after winning the first three games 11-4, 11-8 and 12-10. Yao, the sixth seed and world No 160, took the fourth 11-4, won the fifth 12-10 and won the last two 11-6 and 11-8 after 54 minutes.

In the girls' doubles semi-final that followed, she and Jiang lost the first two games 13-11 and 14-12 to Japan's Mao Takamori and Aoba Takahashi, then won the next three 11-6, 11-7 and 11-6. The mixed final was Yao's third match of the day, and the only one she lost.
## France beat both fourth seeds

Noirault, 19 and unseeded, lost the first game to Hong Kong's Li Ki Ho 11-7 and then won three games in a row by two points, 11-9, 12-10 and 12-10, before taking the fifth 11-4. He is ranked 254th and plays Australia's Aditya Sareen in the quarter-finals.

Hochart, the 15th seed and world No 227, beat Hong Kong's Su Tsz Tung, the world No 57, 11-9, 11-6, 11-9, 12-14, 11-9. Su took the fourth game 14-12, but Hochart won the fifth 11-9. She now plays Yao.

Both French players also left with bronze medals in the doubles, where semi-final losers share third place. Wen and Li beat Noirault and Nathan Pilard 11-9, 11-3, 11-3 in 17 minutes, the shortest match of the day, and South Korea's top seeds Jeong Yein and Heo Yerim beat Hochart and Alexia Nodin 10-12, 11-8, 11-5, 11-4. The other bronzes went to Takamori and Takahashi and to Kazakhstan's Alan Kurmangaliyev and Iran's Benyamin Faraji, who lost 11-6, 11-6, 11-5 to South Korea's Kim Daehwan and Lee Hyeonho. Iran's WANA news agency said it was the country's first doubles medal at the championships.
## Two Indian girls through in seven games

India's Syndrela Das, the world No 95, beat Taiwan's ninth seed Wu Jia-En 11-9 in the seventh game after 55 minutes, the longest match of the day. Das led 2-0 and 3-2 before Wu forced a seventh game. Divyanshi Bhowmick, the eighth seed, who turned 16 last week, also needed seven games against Poland's Natalia Bogdanowicz, winning the decider 11-5 after losing the fifth and sixth.

Das plays Takamori next. The second seed lost the first game 12-10 to Australia's Constantina Psihogios, the world No 67, then won four in a row, two of them in deuce. Bhowmick meets Egypt's Hana Goda, who beat Heo 11-8, 11-1, 11-9, 11-2 and dropped 20 points.
## The home player goes out

Turkey's Kenan Kahraman, 16, took the first game 14-12 from Taiwan's Hung Che-Yen and lost the next four. Hung, the 12th seed, now plays Wen in a rematch of the deciding match of Monday's boys' team final, which Wen won in five games.

Wen dropped 15 points against Puerto Rico's ninth seed Steven Moreno in 21 minutes, and Jiang beat France's Alexia Nodin 11-8, 11-8, 11-8, 11-5. Colombia's second seed Emanuel Otalvaro beat India's Priyanuj Bhattacharyya 11-6, 13-11, 11-3, 11-5, and Li beat Italy's Francesco Trevisan in five, which sets up the rematch of their Youth Olympic Games quarter-final in Dakar, [where Otalvaro won](/news/youth-olympic-games-dakar-2026-otalvaro-beats-li-hechen-china-no-medal.html). Japan's Shunto Iwaida swept India's eighth seed Abhinandh Pradhivadhi, and Tunisia's Wassim Essid beat Australia's Chulong Nie 4-1, winning two games 12-10.

## Friday: quarter-finals and two doubles finals

The singles quarter-finals start at about 11am UK time with Wen against Hung and Das against Takamori. Li plays Otalvaro and Hochart plays Yao at about 11.45am, Iwaida plays Essid and Jiang plays Taiwan's fifth seed Wu Ying Syuan at about 12.30pm, and Bhowmick plays Goda and Noirault plays Sareen at about 1.15pm.

The girls' doubles final, Jeong and Heo against Jiang and Yao, is at about 4pm, and the boys' doubles final, Wen and Li against Kim and Lee, follows at about 4.30pm. Times are approximate. Eleven's [event page](/events/world-youth-championships-2026.html#matches) has live scores and the draws, and the [day six preview](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-day-six-preview-order-of-play.html) has more on the players.
